headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are largely absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents a shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser relationship. Agent A is content-writing with network egress none; agent B is game-playing with network egress none. With no ingest path from A to B or vice versa, prompt injection is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste channels.
Do not mount a common workspace for both agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, both have network egress set to none, and no shared workspace or OAuth principal is documented. That makes a leakage pathway from one agent to the other or to a third party unsupported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later given access to sensitive files or outbound network access, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Review any future OAuth or API scopes before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither profile exposes write capabilities, mutable shared resources, or concurrency primitives. Agent A is runnable false and agent B is runnable false, so there is no documented overlapping write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF either agent is made runnable with shared write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk becomes relevant.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in the current deployment.
Do not grant shared write access to any filesystem or database.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where B consumes A's outputs, and neither profile shows downstream action authority. A is content-writing and B is game-playing, but without an explicit handoff or verification gap, cascading error is not evidenced.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A's text as authoritative input, this risk becomes active.
mitigations: Require human review before any handoff between agents.
Do not auto-feed A's outputs into B.
requires-engineering: add validation if a pipeline is later created.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Agent A and B both show no touched data classes, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document residency and retention before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy controls if regulated data use is planned.
